iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State short vs long reads, de Bruijn assembly, and the N50 metric.
agents.II: Derive the de Bruijn graph for a read set and the N50 computation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Compeau, Pevzner, Tesler 2011; Goodwin et al. 2016.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline variant interpretation (field 292). Trap: must not claim an assembly is complete without T2T evidence.

agents.I: State synteny, orthology, paralogy, and genome duplications.
agents.II: Derive an orthology-inference algorithm from sequence similarity and synteny.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Koonin, Orthologs, Paralogs, and Evolutionary Genomics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline phylogenetics (field 293). Trap: must not claim similarity alone establishes orthology.

agents.I: State pooled vs arrayed screens and sgRNA libraries; hit calling.
agents.II: Derive the hit-calling statistics for a pooled screen and the FDR control.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shalem et al. 2014; Doench 2018.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline genome editing (field 291). Trap: must not claim a screen hit is a validated target.

agents.I: State RNA-seq quantification, differential expression, and batch effects.
agents.II: Derive the negative-binomial model of DESeq2 and its shrinkage estimator.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Love, Huber, Anders 2014 (DESeq2).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline single-cell (field 287). Trap: must not claim a DE gene is causal.

agents.I: State bottom-up proteomics, peptide-spectrum matching, and FDR.
agents.II: Derive the target-decoy FDR estimation and the q-value.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Aebersold & Mann 2003; Nesvizhskii 2010.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline metabolomics (field 286). Trap: must not claim abundance ratios without normalization.

agents.I: State NMR vs LC-MS platforms and metabolite annotation.
agents.II: Derive the isotope-pattern matching score for annotation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wishart 2016; Dunn et al. 2011.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline proteomics (field 285). Trap: must not claim a feature's identity without standards.

agents.I: State droplet scRNA-seq, the UMAP/leiden pipeline, and dropouts.
agents.II: Derive the negative-binomial dropout model and the normalization of scRNA-seq counts.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Zheng et al. 2017; Stuart et al. 2019 (Seurat).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline bulk RNA-seq (field 284). Trap: must not claim clusters are cell types without markers.

agents.I: State ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq and peak calling.
agents.II: Derive the MACS2 peak-calling statistics and the q-value.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Landt et al. 2012 (ENCODE guidelines).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline chromatin biology (field 269). Trap: must not claim a peak implies regulation.

agents.I: State Boolean vs ODE models, parameter estimation, and attractors.
agents.II: Derive the steady states of a Boolean network and its attractor structure.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Alon, An Introduction to Systems Biology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline statistical inference (field 45). Trap: must not claim a fitted model predicts outside its training perturbations.

agents.I: State alignment (BWA) and variant calling (GATK); VCF quality.
agents.II: Derive the Burrows-Wheeler alignment and the HaplotypeCaller likelihood.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Li & Durbin 2009; DePristo et al. 2011.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline assembly (field 281). Trap: must not claim a called variant is true without validation.

agents.I: State Cas9 targeting (PAM, guide design) and repair outcomes (HDR/NHEJ).
agents.II: Derive the guide-RNA targeting specificity and the off-target scoring.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Jinek et al. 2012; Hsu et al. 2014.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline screens (field 283). Trap: must not claim editing is scar-free or perfectly specific.

agents.I: State Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, selection coefficients, and linkage disequilibrium.
agents.II: Derive the allele-frequency change under selection and the fixation probability.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gillespie, Population Genetics: A Concise Guide.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical genetics (field 268). Trap: must not assume neutrality without tests.

agents.I: State substitution models, tree inference (ML/Bayesian), and bootstrap support.
agents.II: Derive the JC69 likelihood and the maximum-parsimony objective.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Felsenstein, Inferring Phylogenies.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline comparative genomics (field 282). Trap: must not claim a supported clade is biologically meaningful.

agents.I: State shotgun vs 16S, taxonomic assignment, and compositional bias.
agents.II: Derive the compositional data analysis (CLR transform) for relative abundances.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Quince et al. 2017; Knight et al. 2018.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical claims (field 320). Trap: must not claim relative abundances are absolute or causal.

agents.I: State somatic variant calling, clonal evolution, and driver vs passenger.
agents.II: Derive the clonal-deconvolution model from variant allele frequencies.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Stratton et al. 2009; Vogelstein et al. 2013.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical oncology (field 313). Trap: must not claim a recurrently mutated gene is a driver.

agents.I: State population coding, receptive fields, and cortical columns.
agents.II: Derive the population vector decoder and its accuracy from tuning curves.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science; Dayan & Abbott.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cellular mechanisms (field 307). Trap: must not claim one neuron's response defines perception.

agents.I: State integrate-and-fire and rate models; Hopfield networks.
agents.II: Derive the leaky integrate-and-fire response and the Hopfield energy function.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dayan & Abbott, Theoretical Neuroscience.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ML theory (field 63). Trap: must not claim a model neuron captures biological detail.

agents.I: State rate vs temporal coding and information-theoretic measures.
agents.II: Derive the mutual information between a stimulus and a spike train.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rieke et al., Spikes: Exploring the Neural Code.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline decision making (field 301). Trap: must not claim mutual information implies readout.

agents.I: State Hebbian learning, LTP/LTD, and critical periods.
agents.II: Derive the BCM rule and its stability properties.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Malenka & Bear 2004; Bliss & Lomo 1973.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cognitive memory (field 300). Trap: must not claim LTP alone explains memory.

agents.I: State working memory, attention networks, and double dissociations.
agents.II: Derive the biased-competition model of attention.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gazzaniga, Ivry, Mangun, Cognitive Neuroscience.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline psychometrics (field 425). Trap: must not claim fMRI activation equals necessity.

agents.I: State drift-diffusion models and value-based choice.
agents.II: Derive the drift-diffusion model's error rate and decision-time distributions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gold & Shadlen 2007; Kable & Glimcher 2009.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline behavioral economics (field 376). Trap: must not claim a model fit implies the brain computes that algorithm.

agents.I: State internal models, the cerebellum's role, and efference copy.
agents.II: Derive the optimal-feedback-control model of reaching.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wolpert et al. 1998; Shadmehr & Wise.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline robotics control (field 128). Trap: must not claim the brain stores explicit inverse-dynamics tables.

agents.I: State the retina-to-V1 pathway and orientation selectivity.
agents.II: Derive the Gabor-receptive-field model and its spatial-frequency tuning.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hubel & Wiesel 1962; Wandell.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline computer vision (field 91). Trap: must not claim V1 responses are the whole percept.

agents.I: State cochlear tonotopy, the superior olive, and spectrotemporal receptive fields.
agents.II: Derive the interaural-time-difference codec and its acuity limit.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Pickles, An Introduction to the Physiology of Hearing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline speech technology (field 115). Trap: must not claim a fiber's tuning fully explains perception.

agents.I: State the Hodgkin-Huxley action potential and patch clamp; field potentials.
agents.II: Derive the Hodgkin-Huxley equations and the action-potential threshold.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hille, Ion Channels of Excitable Membranes.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline imaging (field 306). Trap: must not claim an extracellular spike is reliably one neuron.

agents.I: State BOLD's physiological basis, EEG source ambiguity, and multiple comparisons.
agents.II: Derive the general linear model of fMRI analysis and the hemodynamic response.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Huettel, Song, McCarthy, Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical radiology (field 327). Trap: must not claim BOLD activation is directly neural firing.

agents.I: State synaptic transmission, receptor types, and ionotropic vs metabotropic.
agents.II: Derive the quantal release model (binomial) of synaptic transmission.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline plasticity (field 299). Trap: must not claim an antagonist's effect is purely postsynaptic.

agents.I: State neurogenesis, circuit refinement (pruning), and critical periods.
agents.II: Derive the activity-dependent competition model of synaptic refinement.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sanes, Reh, Harris, Development of the Nervous System.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline adult plasticity (field 299). Trap: must not claim developmental mechanisms continue unchanged in adults.

agents.I: State the SCN clock, clock genes, sleep stages, and homeostatic drive.
agents.II: Derive the two-process model of sleep regulation and its phase relationships.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Borbely 1982; Takahashi et al. 2008.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical sleep medicine (field 315). Trap: must not claim a clock-gene knockout abolishes all rhythmicity.

agents.I: State dopamine/acetylcholine systems and TMS/DBS mechanisms.
agents.II: Derive the cable-model response of a neuron to TMS-induced fields.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Peterchev et al. 2012 (TMS).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline pharmacology (field 338). Trap: must not claim DBS is a simple on/off switch.

agents.I: State predictive coding, hierarchical inference, and precision weighting.
agents.II: Derive the free-energy objective of predictive coding and its update rules.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Friston 2005; Knill & Pouget 2004.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline psychophysics (field 426). Trap: must not claim Bayesian optimality implies explicit posterior computation.

agents.I: State the cardiac cycle, ECG segments, and ejection fraction.
agents.II: Derive the Frank-Starling relationship and the pressure-volume loop of the cardiac cycle.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Braunwald's Heart Disease.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cardiac surgery (field 325). Trap: must not claim a biomarker alone diagnoses MI.

agents.I: State TNM staging, treatment modalities, and complete response.
agents.II: Derive the tumor-growth kinetics model and the log-kill hypothesis.
agents.III: Situate the theory: DeVita, Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cancer genomics (field 295). Trap: must not claim in-vitro response predicts patient response.

agents.I: State NIHSS, thrombolysis windows, and time-since-onset urgency.
agents.II: Derive the ischemic-core growth model and the treatment time window.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ropper & Samuels, Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline psychiatry (field 315). Trap: must not claim imaging alone rules out TIA.

agents.I: State DSM-5 criteria and the limits of the monoamine hypothesis.
agents.II: Derive the receptor-occupancy model of antipsychotic dosing.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Stahl, Essential Psychopharmacology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline neurophysiology (field 305). Trap: must not claim a neurotransmitter imbalance fully explains a disorder.

agents.I: State the HPA/HPT/HPG axes, negative feedback, and HbA1c.
agents.II: Derive the glucose-insulin feedback model and the homeostasis threshold.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cellular metabolism (field 279). Trap: must not claim one hormone level diagnoses a disorder.

agents.I: State GI secretion/absorption, liver function tests, and MELD.
agents.II: Derive the MELD score and its mortality prediction model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sleisenger and Fordtran's GI and Liver Disease.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline bariatric surgery (field 325). Trap: must not claim a liver enzyme elevation equals liver failure.

agents.I: State spirometry interpretation and the P/F ratio.
agents.II: Derive the alveolar gas equation and the shunt equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Murray & Nadel's Textbook of Respiratory Medicine.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline critical care (field 329). Trap: must not claim a CXR finding is pathogen-diagnostic.

agents.I: State GFR estimation, nephron functions, and acid-base compensation.
agents.II: Derive the creatinine-clearance formula and the renal acid-base handling.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Brenner & Rector's The Kidney.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline dialysis engineering (field 484). Trap: must not claim creatinine alone estimates GFR accurately.

agents.I: State transmission dynamics, diagnostic gold standards, and R0.
agents.II: Derive R0 from the next-generation matrix of an SIR model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mandell, Douglas, and Bennett's Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline public health (field 330). Trap: must not claim a PCR positive equals active infection.

agents.I: State hypersensitivity types I-IV and immunodeficiency evaluation.
agents.II: Derive the RAST inhibition curve for allergen-specific IgE quantitation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rich et al., Clinical Immunology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline molecular immunology (field 277). Trap: must not claim a skin test alone proves clinical allergy.

agents.I: State ANA and antibody panels' predictive value; classification criteria.
agents.II: Derive the likelihood-ratio interpretation of an antibody panel.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kelley and Firestein's Textbook of Rheumatology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline molecular autoimmunity (field 277). Trap: must not claim a positive ANA diagnoses lupus.

agents.I: State growth charts, developmental milestones, and jaundice thresholds.
agents.II: Derive the bilirubin phototherapy threshold from the hour-specific nomogram.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline adult medicine (field 312). Trap: must not claim pediatric doses scale linearly from adults.

agents.I: State menstrual-cycle hormonal control and pregnancy trimesters.
agents.II: Derive the Bishop-score prediction of induction success.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Williams Obstetrics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline maternal-fetal procedures (field 325). Trap: must not claim a fetal heart tracing alone determines well-being.

agents.I: State the perioperative pathway, asepsis, and Clavien-Dindo grading.
agents.II: Derive the wound-healing time course and the infection-risk model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Schwartz's Principles of Surgery.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline anesthesia (field 326). Trap: must not claim a surgical outcome is operator-independent.

agents.I: State ASA classification, anesthetic depth, and the difficult-airway algorithm.
agents.II: Derive the pharmacokinetic model of volatile-agent uptake.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Miller's Anesthesia.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline critical care (field 329). Trap: must not claim a drug's clearance is fixed across patients.

agents.I: State modality physics (CT dose, MRI sequences) and ALARA.
agents.II: Derive the CT dose index and the MRI signal equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Brant & Helms, Fundamentals of Diagnostic Radiology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline image analysis (field 99). Trap: must not claim an incidental finding is necessarily significant.

agents.I: State tissue processing, IHC's role, and tumor grading.
agents.II: Derive the diagnostic test's sensitivity-specificity trade-off and the Youden index.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline oncology staging (field 313). Trap: must not claim a histologic grade predicts individual prognosis.

agents.I: State the ABCDE approach, shock classification, and the Berlin ARDS definition.
agents.II: Derive the oxygen-delivery equation and the P/F ratio thresholds.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Marino, The ICU Book.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline pulmonology (field 318). Trap: must not claim a single vital sign drives resuscitation decisions.

agents.I: State screening principles (Wilson-Jungner), the prevention paradox, and NNT.
agents.II: Derive the number-needed-to-treat and the lead-time bias in screening.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gordis, Epidemiology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical ID (field 320). Trap: must not claim screening sensitivity translates to population benefit.

agents.I: State randomization, blinding, the CONSORT flow, and hazard ratios.
agents.II: Derive the log-rank test and the Kaplan-Meier estimator.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Friedman et al., Fundamentals of Clinical Trials.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline statistical theory (field 33). Trap: must not claim a subgroup analysis is definitive.
